title: Set Matrix Zeroes

concept.title: Mark first, change later
body: If you set a row and a column to zero right when you see a zero, the new zeros fool the rest of the scan: you would zero out far too much. Instead do two phases. **Phase 1**: read the original matrix and record which rows and which columns contain a zero. **Phase 2**: zero every cell whose row or column is marked.
Separating "decide" from "change" is a general way to avoid mixing old and new values.

statement: Given a matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns, set the whole row and the whole column of every cell that is 0 to 0. Decide based on the original matrix only. Print the new matrix.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` integers each.
outputFormat: Print the matrix, `n` lines with `m` integers each.

examples.note: The zero in the middle clears the second row and the second column.

hints: Do not change the matrix while you are still searching for zeros.
First note which rows and which columns contain a zero.
Then set to 0 every cell in a marked row or a marked column.
